title: Direction Sense
shortDescription: Sketch a coordinate path instead of tracking turns in your head — net displacement and final facing direction come straight off the drawing.
genZNote: North is the main character. Everything else is just trying to figure out where it went — sketch the path, don't narrate it.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.body: Direction sense questions describe a sequence of turns and movements, then ask for the final direction, the net displacement, or the shortest distance back to the start. The reliable method is to sketch a simple coordinate path (treat North as +y, East as +x) rather than tracking turns mentally.

sections.heading: Turning Rules
bullets: Facing North: a right turn faces East, a left turn faces West.
Facing East: a right turn faces South, a left turn faces North.
Facing South: a right turn faces West, a left turn faces East.
Facing West: a right turn faces North, a left turn faces South.
A 180° turn (or two successive same-direction 90° turns) reverses the current facing entirely.

steps.name: Plot the path
steps.explanation: A walks 5 km North, turns right, walks 3 km, turns right again, walks 5 km. Plot on a grid: start (0,0) → (0,5) after walking North → facing East now, walk 3 km → (3,5) → facing South now (right turn from East), walk 5 km → (3,0).
steps.purpose: Each turn and distance becomes a simple coordinate step — no need to visualise the whole path in your head.

steps.name: Read off the answer
steps.explanation: Final position (3,0) vs start (0,0): straight-line distance = 3 km, due East of the start point.
steps.purpose: The displacement and direction are read directly off the two coordinate points.

sections.heading: Common Traps
bullets: Confusing 'turns right' with 'turns to face right of the reader's view' instead of the walker's own current facing direction — always rotate relative to the walker's current heading, not a fixed compass view.
Forgetting that two consecutive right (or left) turns amount to a full reversal, and treating it as still facing perpendicular to the original direction.
Computing distance travelled (sum of all leg lengths) when the question actually asks for straight-line displacement from start to end, or vice versa.

sections.heading: Exam Strategy
bullets: Always sketch on scratch paper with North as up — even a rough grid prevents directional errors.
Re-read whether the question wants final direction, straight-line displacement, or total distance walked — these are three different answers from the same path.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Direction sense questions are solved by plotting turns and distances on a simple coordinate grid rather than tracking them mentally.
keyFacts: Right/left turns rotate relative to the walker's CURRENT facing direction, not a fixed compass view.
Two same-direction 90° turns equal a full 180° reversal.
Straight-line displacement and total distance walked are different quantities — check which one is asked.
commonConfusion: Turning right always means right relative to where the person is currently facing, not a fixed map direction.

highYieldFacts: Plotting each leg on a North-up coordinate grid removes almost all direction-tracking errors.
commonTraps: Answering with total path length when straight-line displacement was asked, or vice versa.
mustRemember: Right/left turns are always relative to the walker's current facing direction.
